A final long vowel generally carries the stress, but there are many exceptions in the texts which may be due to inexact notation. In groups of numerals the second is stressed. E.g. i:d'u: apta one or two weeks; trä č'air du: three or four days; cha s'asta mai six ... usually stressed; thus sa:i/pu:tr t'a:nuk his own sister/son. In some cases an especially ... stress, accompanied by a high tone, was recorded. E.g. n"andəma:la:a; n"andi:; č'üikai 193,6; cf. also 193,9,10; 194,5; 21,13; 87,8; 104,4; 120,2,14. But also in ordinary pronunciation the stressed syllable usually had a high tone. A low, rising tone was characteristic of words with original voiced aspirate. Thus, dhár hill, but darr [scan; da:r] wood (level, or falling tone); gór'a: horse, but go:l'an cow. The relation between tone and aspiration, however, was less easily ... SE. dialects ... I became aware of it too late to be able to make a thorough investigation of it. 2,1. CONSONANTS" (same chapter, sec. 1,7: "Quantity is phonemically relevant.")

new_statements.rule_in_words: In SW Pashai, word stress generally falls on the final long vowel of the word (vowel length is phonemic, sec. 1,7); Morgenstierne flags many exceptions in his texts, possibly notational. In numeral groups ('one or two', 'three or four') the second numeral is stressed. Stressed syllables normally carry high pitch; words with a historical voiced aspirate have a low rising tone instead (dhár 'hill' vs da:r 'wood'), i.e. an incipient tonal contrast tied to aspiration.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing in the recovered SW-group text. (Morgenstierne 1944, Texts vol., intro snippet: 'In a few cases secondary stress has been noted in polysyllabics (ˈādamana "by the men")' -- notation remark, not a rule.)
new_statements.exceptions: 'many exceptions in the texts which may be due to inexact notation'; numeral groups stress the second member; reflexive t'a:nuk 'own' usually stressed after the noun; emphatic extra-strong stress with high tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress as marked in Morgenstierne's field transcriptions and texts (SW group informants: Tagau etc.); statement is quantity-driven (last LONG vowel), so words without a long vowel are not covered by the recovered text. Grjunberg's identical rule is stated for Pashai as a whole, with his phoneme inventories explicitly those of the SW zone.
new_statements.identity_note: Morgenstierne 1967's 'SW. Group' chapter is exactly the ISO psh / Glottolog sout2671 unit (Tagau/Tagab, Ishpi, Isken; Quasnik 2019 adds Alasai, Kapisa as the psh sample point). Grjunberg 1999 states the same rule for Pashai as a whole (all four groups) but bases his phoneme inventories explicitly on the south-western zone. Sibling-variety statements held by the project: NE Pashayi Kordar (kurd1258 under nort2666) 'stress generally word-final' (Nawata 1985 p.161); SE Pashayi (sout2672) prosody undescribed (Lamuwal & Baker 2013) / lexical pitch accent (Strand, Degano).
